title: Guardrail layers and summarized proof — PRD (rough)
content:
Context / why this exists:

We keep getting requests from customers who want: (a) minimal telemetry shipped back to Redwood for compliance review, (b) strong customer-side evidence that their VPC/networking/changes were accepted and applied, and (c) a frictionless approval UX for delegated operators. Current PRDs in this bucket focus on very verbose attestation/forensic bundles — good for deep investigations, but heavy for day-to-day authorization flows and incompatible with low-bandwidth or privacy-sensitive customers.

This doc sketches a complementary approach: two related ideas — "approval rings" (a layered guardrail model for runbook/AO authorization) and "summarized proof" (compact, verifiable audit artifacts designed to minimize PII and size while preserving forensic value). Goal is a pragmatic, rollout-friendly design suitable for Private deployments (customer-managed networking, VPC handoff) and Redwood Private control plane integrations.

Problem statement:
- Customers want a small, signed artifact they can store and query cheaply for compliance and handovers.
- Operators want to reduce cognitive overhead: fewer fields, clear pass/fail signals, and built-in remediation links.
- Redwood wants to retain sufficient telemetry for platform health and regressions without collecting unnecessary private payloads.

Goals (high level):
- Define approval rings UX and API (customer operator -> delegated operator -> Redwood concierge) with clear escalation semantics.
- Define a compact audit artifact ("summarized proof") that:
  - is cryptographically signed (customer and Redwood where applicable),
  - contains immutable metadata required for audits (change id, decision, signer ids, evidence digest),
  - includes a small, optional human-readable summary and a retention pointer to richer evidence (stored only if explicitly enabled).
- Provide migration path and acceptance criteria for pilot customers.

Non-goals:
- This is not a full replacement for existing detailed forensic bundles — those remain available for high-fidelity investigations and legal requests.
- Not addressing deep SIEM/enterprise correlation pipelines here — only the compact artifact shape and handoff UX.

Proposed design overview — Approval Rings:
- Concept: think of approvals as concentric rings of trust and remediation responsibilities. Each ring represents a set of identity principals and one action policy. Rings are ordered from closest-to-customer to Redwood-managed.
- Example rings:
  - Ring 0: Customer owner/manual confirmation (e.g., a named engineer or oncall).
  - Ring 1: Delegated operator or operator group (customer-managed operator service account).
  - Ring 2: Automated guardrail (preflight checks, linting, compliance policy), returns CLEAR/FLAGGED with suggested fixes.
  - Ring 3: Redwood concierge fallback (limited emergency approval channel with strict SLAs and evidence requirements).
- Each approval event records: ring_id, decision (approve/deny/escalate), signer, timestamp, decision_ttl (how long this decision is considered valid for incremental changes).
- Escalation behavior: ring must explicitly pass before next ring can act; however, we allow "fast-path" where an operator from Ring 1 can append an "override token" when preconditions satisfied (policy-based).

Compact artifact: "summarized proof" schema (proposal) — designed to be intentionally terse:
- fields (flat):
  - change_id: short uuid
  - summary: single-line human text (max 280 chars)
  - decision: APPROVE | DENY | ESCALATE | AUTO_PASS
  - ring_trace: comma-separated ring ids with chronological signer handles (e.g., R0:maya.c,R1:ops-team-2)
  - evidence_digest: base64url(SHA256(rich_evidence_blob)) or empty if not stored
  - storage_pointer: optional signed pointer (url or object id) to richer evidence on customer-controlled storage or Redwood escrow
  - signatures: comma-separated signatures using key IDs (customer_key:v1,redwood_key:v1)
  - ts: ISO-8601 timestamp
  - retention_policy: short tag (e.g., rp:30d, rp:365d, rp:ephemeral)
  - change_category: egress-rule|route|dns|keystore|operator-config
  - verification_hint: short status (VALID|MISMATCH|MISSING_PTR)

Why this shape?
- Flat fields map cleanly to CSV/search indexes; small payload ensures cheap storage and fast queries.
- A digest + pointer gives auditors ability to require a deeper bundle on demand while keeping the usual data path lightweight.
- Signatures permit later verification without revealing sensitive data in the summary itself.

Operator UX and on-screen affordances:
- Change card in Console: single-line summary + trust bar showing rings completed (visual rings fill left-to-right). Click expands full ring_trace and signatures.
- Quick rollback button when decision within the last X minutes and last signer belongs to Ring 0 or Ring 1.
- A lightweight "evidence retrieval" flow that performs a verified challenge to retrieve the rich bundle from customer storage (requires keys/consent).

API contract (sketch):
- POST /private/v1/changes (payload: change metadata, optional evidence pointer). Returns change_id and a draft summarized proof with provisional signature.
- POST /private/v1/changes/{id}/approve?ring={n} (payload: signer_id, signer_key_sig, short reason). Returns updated summarized_proof and event id.
- GET /private/v1/changes/{id}/proof (returns summarized_proof).
- GET /private/v1/changes/{id}/evidence?mode=verify (performs signed verification handshake and returns pointer or 403).

Retention, privacy and minimal telemetry rules:
- Default behavior in Private deployments: only summarized_proof artifacts are stored in Redwood control plane for 30 days (rp:30d) unless customer explicit opt-in sets longer retention.
- Evidence blobs (richer logs, full stack traces, packet captures) are kept ONLY on customer-managed storage unless customer checks a box to escrow with Redwood for X days. If escrowed, the summarized_proof must contain the evidence_digest and a signed storage_pointer.
- PII minimization: summaries must exclude raw IPs, user tokens, or full request bodies. Any attempt to POST such fields should return 400 with guidance.

Verification and audit flows:
- Verification is two-step: (1) check summarized_proof signatures and evidence_digest, (2) optionally request richer evidence from storage_pointer and confirm the digest matches.
- Archive-friendly: for long-term legal holds, customers can store summarized_proofs plus the escrowed evidence bundle (if they elected escrow) in an immutable archive and provide an index.

Migration plan and pilot strategy:
- Phase 0 (internal validation): implement API stubs and Console UI mock; test across 2 pilot customers in staging with varying bandwidth constraints.
- Phase 1 (opt-in pilot): a handful of early Private customers are invited; default retention set to 30d; gather feedback on ring definitions and rollback rules.
- Phase 2 (broad opt-in): exposure in Console with a migration assistant that converts existing verbose bundles to summarized_proofs + evidence digest pointers.

Acceptance criteria (example):
- Pilot customers can complete a change and obtain a summarized_proof that verifies against the richer evidence bundle in >95% of retrieval attempts (network/timeouts excluded).
- UI shows ring progress and allows rollback for at least Ring 0/Ring 1 decisions within 15 minutes.
- Summarized_proof sizes average <1KB and indexing latency under 200ms for reads in the control plane.

Open questions / unresolved tradeoffs:
- How many ring levels do we expose as configurable vs. fixed? (Configurable is flexible but increases surface for customer error.)
- Key management: do we require customer-managed signing keys (recommended) or allow Redwood-hosted signing with customer attestations?
- Emergency overrides: how should compensation/audit work when Redwood concierge issues a Ring 3 approval? (explicit SLA + forensic bundle required?)
- Legal/evidence admissibility: are summarized_proofs acceptable as a primary audit artifact in major customer jurisdictions, or do we need mandatory deeper bundles for certain regulated industries?

Implementation notes / rough tech constraints:
- Keep summarized_proof as a single flat DB row for fast scans. Index on change_id, ts, change_category, decision, signer (or signer hash).
- Evidence pointers can be presigned URLs with short TTL or opaque object ids; when pointing to customer storage, require signed consent token to avoid accidental disclosure.
- Use standard compact signature formats (e.g., COSE/Ed25519) so verification is simple across libs.

Next steps (immediate):
- Product: refine ring defaults and migration UX; collect 3 candidate pilot customers. (owner: Maya)
- Eng: spike a summarized_proof schema and a small in-memory verifier; wire an authentication-only evidence retrieval flow. (owner: Arjun)
- Security/Legal: prepare a short guidance doc about admissibility and recommended key management options. (owner: Lena)
- Schedule a 90-minute cross-team workshop (SRE, Eng, Security, Solutions) to validate rollback guards, retention tags, and emergency approval playbook.

Notes to reviewers (brain-dump style):
- I intentionally kept fields tiny to make this friendly to export into CSV/ELK and to reduce the temptation to fill summaries with sensitive payloads.
- For pilot, we should test 3 real-world scenarios: DNS route change, egress-rule add, and operator keystore rotation — those map to different evidence types and help validate pointer flows.

- End of doc - feedback welcome, will iterate the schema and wireframes after the workshop.
